output_text:
name: python-observability
description: Python structured logging, metrics, and distributed tracing for production debugging.

Use for adding logging, metrics, tracing, correlation IDs, dashboards, or debugging production issues. Emit JSON logs with consistent fields; human-readable logs may suit local development. Track latency, traffic, errors, and saturation at every service boundary. Generate a unique ID at ingress and propagate it through requests, logs, and spans.

Logging: Configure structlog with `structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars`, `structlog.processors.add_log_level`, `structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso")`, `structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer()`, `structlog.processors.format_exc_info`, and `structlog.processors.JSONRenderer()`. Include correlation ID, method, path, user ID, result, duration, and error details where relevant. Use DEBUG for diagnostics, INFO for operations, WARNING for recoverable anomalies, and ERROR for failures needing attention.

Never log expected behavior at `ERROR`. A user entering a wrong password is `INFO`, not `ERROR`.

Correlation: Use `ContextVar` and `structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars`; accept `X-Correlation-ID` or generate `str(uuid.uuid4())`, and return the ID in the response header. Propagate it to outbound requests using `headers={"X-Correlation-ID": correlation_id.get()}`.

Metrics: Use `prometheus_client` Counter, Histogram, and Gauge for request counts, latency, errors, and resource usage. Record method, endpoint, status, and error type as appropriate.

Keep metric label values bounded. Unbounded labels (like user IDs) explode storage costs.
Avoid labels with unbounded values to prevent metric explosion.
Never use unbounded values as metric labels

Use bounded labels such as method, endpoint, status, or a fixed user tier; never use user IDs as labels.

Use `time.perf_counter()` and a reusable context manager to time operations and log duration, including failures.

Tracing: Use OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry.trace`, `TracerProvider`, `BatchSpanProcessor`, `OTLPSpanExporter`) and nested spans with useful attributes. See https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/python/ for current API guidance.

Separate observability from business logic; test logs and metrics in integration tests and set up alerts.
